strategies.name: ict_stop_raid_mss_retracement_pd_array_entry
strategies.entry_summary: After establishing directional bias, wait for a liquidity raid/stop raid, then a market structure shift or displacement in the intended direction. Enter on the retracement into discount/premium or OTE where a PD array is present, typically using a fair value gap, order block, breaker block, or a con
strategies.exit_summary: Place the stop beyond the entry structure/PD array or the swept low/high. Take a first partial at opposing liquidity or the initial target level, then either move the stop to breakeven and let the rest run or continue targeting further liquidity.

strategies.name: ict_box_setup_deviation_retest_reversal
strategies.entry_summary: Use a range-deviation box setup: after price deviates below the range and reclaims back into it, treat that as manipulation and enter on the retest of the manipulation area for a move to the opposite side of the range. This setup is presented as valid even without the prior lower-timeframe stop-raid
strategies.exit_summary: Take partials as price moves toward the opposite side of the range and continue holding for liquidity resting beyond that side. Stop is implied beneath the retest/manipulation area.

result.enumeration_note: Two distinct strategy skeletons are taught: the main stop-raid + MSS + retracement into PD-array model, and a separate box-setup deviation/retest reversal. The various FVG/order-block/breaker/OTE examples within the first are compatible entry-model variants, not separate strategies.
